Time and memory by modeling task

Colocad candidate b3e6000, CadQuery 2.8.0 and build123d 0.13.0. On the 12 common scaling points, Colocad had the lowest median peak memory in 11/12 and the shortest median wall time in 6/12. These counts give each tested size one vote and are not a distribution of real projects.

One 100-second queue of full hand assemblies

Each job starts a new process. The same ordered edits change guide diameter and cable radius. Count only complete, independently reopened 43-solid STEP handoffs by the deadline. Memory is the largest 25 ms sample, not a per-job kernel peak. One window per backend.

Logical writes come from Linux /proc/PID/io at process exit including waited-for children. Retained files include Colocad checkpoints but exclude instrumentation and supplied inputs. Warm-cache block counters on a host bind mount cannot establish physical SSD bandwidth. All three tools are tested on real edits; there is no claim of universal CAD API parity.

These paired builds use 64 independently dimensioned plates with 16 bores each. Each occurrence still undergoes Level‑1 and manifold checks. Certified quadratic trim spans and reused pure spline analyses reduce repeated numerical searches. OCCT read back the same STEP bytes on both sides.

The separate write experiment executed 100 edits and 9,900 queries. Each recorded receipt and accepted geometry hash was checked after reopening the project.

Memory across all twelve scaling points

STEP readbacks at the same camera and scale

Six macOS arm64 controls, five fresh builds per case and backend. Colocad and build123d 0.11.1 use their original independent implementations. The figures report median wall time and maximum process RSS.
